question: Who among the following was the first chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Vikram A Sarabhai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Vikram A Sarabhai** was the **founder and the first chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, established in **1969**. He is regarded as the father of the Indian space program.
 
• He played a pivotal role in establishing the **Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR)** in **1962**, which later evolved into ISRO.
 
• Dr. Sarabhai's vision was to use **space technology for socio-economic development**. He emphasized the importance of using satellites for communication, education, and agricultural development in India.
 
• Under his leadership, India's first satellite, **Aryabhata**, was conceptualized, although it was launched later in **1975**.
 
• He collaborated with global space agencies, including **NASA**, to set up the **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)** in Kerala for launching sounding rockets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. Vikram A Sarabhai:**

 
 
• Born on **12 August 1919**, in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, he belonged to a prominent industrialist family.
 
• He was instrumental in setting up several scientific institutions in India, including the **Physical Research Laboratory (PRL)** in Ahmedabad in **1947**.
 
• He also contributed to the development of **India's nuclear power program** and worked closely with **Homi J Bhabha**.
 
• Dr. Sarabhai received several accolades, including the **Padma Bhushan (1966)** and **Padma Vibhushan (posthumously in 1972)**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**
 
 
• ISRO was established in **1969** under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). It became a part of the **Department of Space** in **1972**.
 
• ISRO's primary objective is to develop space technology and use its applications for various national tasks.
 
• It has launched numerous satellites like **INSAT**, **GSAT**, and **RISAT** for communication, weather forecasting, and remote sensing.
 
• ISRO's achievements include the **Mangalyaan mission (Mars Orbiter Mission, 2013)** and the **Chandrayaan missions** to the Moon.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Prof. M G K Menon:** He was a renowned physicist who served as the Chairman of the Indian Space Commission but not the first chairman of ISRO.
 
• **Prof. Satish Dhawan:** He succeeded Dr. Sarabhai as the Chairman of ISRO in **1972** and contributed significantly to its growth, including the launch of the first Indian satellite, **Aryabhata**.
 
• **Homi J Bhabha:** Known as the **father of the Indian nuclear program**, he was instrumental in the establishment of atomic energy research in India but was not directly involved with ISRO.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **First Satellite:** India's first satellite, **Aryabhata**, was launched on **19 April 1975**, from the Soviet Union. It marked a significant milestone in India's space journey.
 
• **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS):** Established in **1963**, TERLS was India's first rocket launching station, located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
 
• **INSAT Series:** The Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system, launched in the 1980s, is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• **Vision of Dr. Sarabhai:** He believed in using space technology for **developmental purposes** rather than military or competitive aspirations.
